validated_results.title: Long-term supplementation of decaffeinated green tea extract does not modify body weight or abdominal obesity in a randomized trial of men at high risk for prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: This randomized trial of decaffeinated green tea catechins reported only obesity biomarkers (weight, BMI, waist:hip ratio) in men at high risk, with no prostate cancer incidence results.

validated_results.title: Long-term supplementation of decaffeinated green tea extract does not modify body weight or abdominal obesity in a randomized trial of men at high risk for prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: The trial's outcomes were anthropometric obesity biomarkers rather than incident prostate cancer, so no prostate cancer incidence estimate is available.

validated_results.title: The effects of Curcuma longa and curcumin on reproductive systems.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative literature review of Curcuma longa and curcumin effects on reproductive organs, not an original human study of turmeric and prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Epigenetic Changes Induced by Green Tea Catechins a re Associated with Prostate Cancer.
validated_results.reason: The article is a review summarizing epigenetic and miRNA effects of green tea catechins in prostate cancer without original human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Epigenetic Changes Induced by Green Tea Catechins a re Associated with Prostate Cancer.
validated_results.reason: The article explicitly states it will "summarize the key results from recent studies", making it a review rather than an original study.

validated_results.title: Plasma Fatty Acids as Surrogate for Prostate Levels.
validated_results.reason: This study only correlated plasma and prostate tissue phospholipid fatty acid concentrations as biomarker validation, providing no evidence on developing prostate cancer.

validated_results.title: Plasma Fatty Acids as Surrogate for Prostate Levels.
validated_results.reason: The analysis assessed surrogacy of plasma fatty acid measures for prostate tissue levels in prostatectomy patients without any prostate cancer incidence outcome.

validated_results.title: Lifestyle Risk Prediction Model for Prostate Cancer in a Korean Population.
validated_results.reason: Large prospective Korean cohort of cancer-free men reporting an alcohol-specific hazard ratio for incident prostate cancer.

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 1,179,172 Korean men who were cancer free from 1996 to 1997, had taken a physical examination, and completed a lifestyle questionnaire, were enrolled in our study to predict their risk for PC for the next eight years, using the Cox proportional hazards model.

effect_size.excerpt: The model performed very well (C statistic, 0.887; 95% confidence interval, 0.879 to 0.895) and estimated an elevated PC risk in patients who did not consume alcohol or smoke, compared to heavy alcohol consumers (hazard ratio [HR], 0.78) and current smokers (HR, 0.73) (p < 0.001).
